description: Differential conformance vectors for the operator assetSchema dialect (docs/spec/profile-schema-dialect.md). The server guard/compiler and the offline signer compiler MUST both produce the stated 'expect' (accept = schema compiles, reject = schema refused) for every case. Parity is a release gate. 'schema' is a full assetSchema document.

cases.name: const-value-with-schema-like-data
cases.note: const value is opaque data, not a schema; keys inside it are not walked

cases.name: enum-value-with-schema-like-data
cases.note: enum values are opaque data

cases.name: local-ref-into-defs
cases.note: $ref is sole member of its object; target lives in $defs

cases.name: reject-oneOf
cases.note: composition

cases.name: reject-multipleOf
cases.note: multipleOf is outside the dialect allowlist

cases.name: reject-format
cases.note: format is outside the dialect allowlist

cases.name: reject-unknown-keyword
cases.note: closed allowlist rejects any unknown key

cases.name: reject-nested-forbidden
cases.note: forbidden keyword deep in the tree

cases.name: reject-ref-with-sibling-validation
cases.note: $ref must be sole member

cases.name: reject-ref-with-sibling-annotation
cases.note: $ref must be sole member even next to an annotation

cases.name: reject-ref-cycle-direct
cases.note: self-referential schema

cases.name: reject-empty-type-array
cases.note: an empty type array is refused

cases.name: reject-defs-unused-forbidden-keyword
cases.note: every $defs member must satisfy the dialect even if never $ref'd

cases.name: accept-defs-unused-valid
cases.note: an unused-but-valid $defs member compiles

cases.name: reject-draft04-boolean-exclusiveMinimum
cases.note: $schema is an annotation with no effect, so the schema is read as this dialect and exclusiveMinimum must be a number

cases.name: accept-schema-draft04-inert
cases.note: $schema selects no draft

cases.name: accept-schema-unknown-uri-inert
cases.note: an unknown metaschema URI is neither fetched nor refused

cases.name: accept-schema-and-id-any-value
cases.note: $schema and $id have no effect, whatever their value

cases.name: accept-nested-id-does-not-rebase-ref
cases.note: #/ pointers resolve from the document root even inside a subschema that carries an $id

cases.name: reject-ref-into-array
cases.note: a pointer descends through objects only

cases.name: reject-ref-percent-encoded
cases.note: the server's compiler would decode %20 and read the integer definition while a literal lookup finds the string one, so '%' is refused

cases.name: reject-ref-cycle-through-defs-of-target
cases.note: a definition nested in the target of a $ref that refers back to that target is a cycle

cases.name: reject-ref-diamond-fan-out
cases.note: 24 levels of definitions that each refer twice to the next expand to more than 10,000 schema nodes; both sides stop at that cap instead of taking exponential time

cases.name: reject-minLength-fraction-form
cases.note: length and count keywords are plain integer literals; 1.0 and 1e1 are refused

cases.name: reject-minimum-unrepresentable-exponent
cases.note: the exponent is too small for an exact rational, so the compiler would drop the bound

limits.note: Mirror of shared/schemas/structural-limits.json. Both binaries enforce EXACTLY these.

instanceCases.name: integer-accepts-subulp-fraction
instanceCases.note: Numbers are read as the float64 the canonical bytes carry: this one is 1

instanceCases.name: enum-schema-literal-is-exact
instanceCases.note: A number written in the schema keeps its exact value

instanceCases.name: property-named-schema-keyword-is-enforced
instanceCases.note: $id and $schema are ignored only as keywords; a property or definition with that name is not a keyword

instanceCases.name: const-keeps-schema-keyword-members-valid
instanceCases.note: const holds data, so its $id and $schema members stay

instanceCases.name: ref-to-key-with-control-character
instanceCases.note: a pointer is literal apart from the ~0 and ~1 escapes, so it finds a key holding a control character

limitCases.name: string-length
limitCases.note: Build assetSchema data = a JSON string of exactly `limit` UTF-8 BYTES (accept) and `limit`+1 bytes (reject) validated against {type:string}, using single-byte (ASCII) characters so byte length and rune count coincide. Both binaries construct identically. The unit is UTF-8 bytes; see string-length-2byte/-3byte/-4byte for multi-byte value vectors and object-key-length/-4byte for the same bound applied to an object key.

limitCases.name: string-length-2byte
limitCases.note: A JSON string value built from the 2-byte-UTF-8 character U+00E9 (é), repeated as many whole times as fit and padded with single-byte 'x' filler, so the value's total UTF-8 BYTE length is exactly `limit` (accept) / `limit`+1 (reject); its rune count is far below `limit`. A value well under `limit` runes but at or over `limit` bytes must be rejected, so length is counted in bytes, not runes.

limitCases.name: string-length-3byte
limitCases.note: Same construction as string-length-2byte using the 3-byte-UTF-8 character U+4E2D (中).

limitCases.name: string-length-4byte
limitCases.note: Same construction as string-length-2byte using the 4-byte-UTF-8 character U+1F600 (😀).

limitCases.name: object-key-length
limitCases.note: A JSON object with a single ASCII key of exactly `limit` bytes (accept) / `limit`+1 bytes (reject). The bound applies to object keys as well as string values, so both binaries check every string token.

limitCases.name: object-key-length-4byte
limitCases.note: Same as object-key-length but the key is built from the 4-byte-UTF-8 character U+1F600 (padded with ASCII 'x'), so its UTF-8 byte length is exactly `limit`/`limit`+1 while its rune count is far smaller. This pins that the key bound is byte-based, not rune-based, like the value bound.

limitCases.name: array-items
limitCases.note: A JSON array of exactly `limit` integers (accept) and `limit`+1 (reject) against {type:array,items:{type:integer}}.

limitCases.name: object-properties
limitCases.note: A JSON object with exactly `limit` string-keyed props (accept) and `limit`+1 (reject) against {type:object}.

limitCases.name: depth
limitCases.note: A JSON value nested exactly `limit` deep (accept) and `limit`+1 deep (reject). Depth = number of nested containers.

limitCases.name: bytes
limitCases.note: A raw JSON document of exactly `limit` uncompressed bytes (accept) and `limit`+1 bytes (reject).

envelopeCases.name: profile-multibyte-names-at-limit
envelopeCases.note: assetType, tokenUnit and recordIdLabel lengths count Unicode code points, as JSON Schema maxLength does, not UTF-8 bytes: 128 x U+00E9, 64 x U+20AC and 128 x U+4E2D sit exactly at their limits.
